To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

different surgical approaches for bilateral ovariectomy and adrenalectomy result in different acute effects on progesterone and estradiol, but not testosterone, serum concentrations in the female rat, and that these effects depend on the day of estrous cycle when the surgery is performed.

acute unilateral or bilateral ovarian or adrenal ablation performed through the dorsal peritoneal wall results in a decrease of progesterone and estradiol, but not testosterone, serum concentrations in the rat.

the acute effects of unilateral or bilateral dorsal surgery for ovariectomy or unilateral or bilateral ventral surgery for adrenalectomy depend on the day of estrous cycle when the surgery is performed and the surgical approach used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the surgical approach and of the estrous stage at the time of surgery on the acute changes in progester-one, testosterone and estradio serum concentrations.
the mechanisms by which the peritoneum or abdominal wall modulates the concentrations of the steroid hormones, progesterone, estradiol and testosterone.
understanding the mechanisms regulating hormone concentrations and their effects in the female and male rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single approach that should be used for all experimental purposes.

the acute effects of bilateral adrenalectomy and ovariectomy on progesterone testosterone and estradiola serum concentrations depend on the surgical technique and the day of estrous cycle when the surgery is performed.

the acute effects of ovariectomy and adrenalectomy performed with a unilateral ventral approach on progesterone and estradiol concentrations depend on the day of estrous cycle when the surgery is performed, whereas the testosterone serum concentrations do not vary with the day of the cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the acute effects of bilateral adrenalectomy or ovariectomy on the serum concentrations of progesterone, androgens and estrogens depend on the day of estrous cycle when it is performed and the surgical approach.
a dorsal approach to perform bilateral ovariectomy results in a greater increase in progesterone serum concentration in animals with a proestrus or estrous than with a diestrus.
the surgical approach to performing bilateral adrenalectomy or ovariectomy has an acute effect on progesterone and testosterone serum concentrations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surgical approach for bilateral ovariectomy and adrenalectomy should be considered when interpreting results from studies using these experimental models.
the surgical approach to perform a bilateral ovariectomy and/or adrenalectomy can affect the acute effects of surgery on hormone serum concentrations.
the surgical approach to performing bilateral adrenalectomy or bilateral ovariectomies can affect hormone serum concentrations and the results obtained from these experimental models.
